title: Small-bias sample
statement: Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $x_0,\ldots,x_{m-1}$ be vectors in the binary cube of dimension $n$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$. The sample is small-biased with bias at most $\varepsilon$ if, for every nonzero binary vector $\gamma$ of length $n$, the absolute value of the empirical mean of the Walsh character indexed by $\gamma$ on the sample is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: The samples are indexed by $\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$ and lie in the binary cube of dimension $n$
The bound applies to every nonzero $\gamma$
